title: Grateful Dead Live at Campolindo High School on 1969-05-16
lineage: Master Soundboard Cassette > Cassette > DAT (speed corrected) > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Hissy gym recording of a ragged high‑school gig where Pigpen shines but the band’s energy falters, with Good Morning Little School Girl and Lovelight as the few bright spots.
ai_review.review: The tape captures a raw, audience‑sourced performance at Campolindo High School that suffers from hissy acoustics, occasional cuts and generally low energy. While Pigpen’s blues numbers and the opening Good Morning Little School Girl plus a decent Lovelight provide highlights, the set is marred by sloppy playing, out‑of‑tune moments and a notorious flop of Hard To Handle. A few reviewers note that recent restoration work improves clarity, but overall the show feels more like a historical curiosity than a must‑listen concert.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviews are split: many give 1–2 stars citing poor performance and hissy sound, while a minority award 4–5 stars for occasional jams and sentimental value. The weighted average lands around 2.8, so the AI rating reflects a mixed but generally below‑average assessment.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Hissy, gym acoustics and occasional cuts (e.g., Lovelight) are noted; some listeners mention that recent cleanup improves clarity, but overall the mix is raw and not well balanced.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set feels uneven, with a sluggish start, a few bright moments in the middle and an abrupt end due to curfew; transitions are not particularly tight.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Often out of tune and lacking passion; occasional nice lines on his Gibson SG; banned from smoking which affected his performance.
band_member_comments.Bob: Credited with rescuing the show, delivering bright guitar work and solid vocals that kept the audience engaged.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen praised for powerful blues singing and organ playing; carries much of the show's momentum.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drummers provide some interesting grooves despite occasional timing issues; Mickey Hart noted as not keeping perfect time but still contributing to the feel.
